evidence.field: A00597; explanation and character citations
evidence.text: The entry states that 哪 is not recorded in Shuowen. It cites Jiyun under 乃箇切 as saying the graph was originally 那, a particle, and sometimes written 哪. It separately records 哪哪 as the sound made by performers in nuo exorcism rites and 咄哪 as a personal name. The entry also describes a copyist’s variant whose middle was changed to 舟 through graphic similarity; this is a corruption within an attested variant, not evidence for the origin of standard 哪.
evidence.title: [A00597] 哪 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00597; explanation and cited forms
evidence.text: The dictionary records the standard graph 哪 with right side 那 and cites later readings and usages: questioning pronoun (which/where) and rhetorical adverb (‘how’). It gives a Qing play citation for the rhetorical use. It reports variant spellings involving 奈 and 舟, but does not document the early palaeographic development of 哪 or establish when the interrogative senses first came to be written with it.
evidence.title: [A00597] 哪 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: A04204; Shuowen explanation and senses of 那
evidence.text: Shuowen analyzes the distinct graph 那 as 邑 semantic plus 冄 phonetic and glosses it as a western non-Chinese polity. The entry also cites Pre-Classical Poetry uses of 那 glossed ‘many’ (桑扈) and ‘tranquil’ (魚藻), and a Zuozhuan use ‘棄甲則那？’ glossed by Du Yu as ‘那 is like 何, what/how’. These are senses and uses of 那, not evidence that the graph 哪 existed in those early texts.
evidence.title: [A04204] 那 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: Kangxi Dictionary section
evidence.text: The entry reproduces Kangxi’s report from Jiyun: 哪 has a reading 乃箇切 and ‘originally was 那’, with 㖠 as another particle spelling; another Jiyun reading labels 哪哪 as the sound of nuo performers. This is later lexicographic testimony, not an excavated early form.

evidence.field: phonetic component analysis; readings and sources
evidence.text: Han Dian classifies 哪 as phonosemantic: 口 plus 那 as sound. It records current Mandarin nǎ, néi, na, né. This modern analysis is consistent with the spelling and sound evidence but does not independently date the compound graph.

gaps: No inspected primary palaeographic corpus/page supplied an oracle-bone, bronze, bamboo, or other early form for 哪. MOE reports it absent from Shuowen; the earliest securely inspected graphic testimony here is later lexicography citing Jiyun, not a dated manuscript witness. Do not assert a graphic chronology beyond that.

The source packet’s competing speech-origin accounts (fusion of 奈何 versus 若何, with ‘which’ possibly from 若) derive from modern scholarship cited through Wiktionary. I did not inspect Wang, Sun, Shimura, or Lü directly, nor the cited Gu Yanwu passage; those etymologies remain competing secondary analyses, and they concern spoken words rather than demonstrated graphic ancestry.

The MOE entry and secondary discussion distinguish earlier 哪 senses (ritual cry, particle, personal name) from later interrogative writing, but this search did not establish a dated first occurrence of 哪 as ‘which/where’. A gloss list alone cannot establish that semantic chronology.

Exact local Unihan_Readings rows were absent for both 哪 and 那 in the checked full/HSK extracts. The official Unicode record for 哪 was opened and cited; the official per-character record for 那 could not be inspected despite direct URL attempts. The official Unicode FAQ explains kMandarin generally, while Wiktionary reports 那 nuó; no claim of exact official/local 那 kMandarin verification is made.

Baxter–Sagart local data contains 那 *nˤar but not a 哪 row. The local file notation was preserved and disagrees with the dossier’s *naːls transcription for 那. No host reconstruction or matched reconstructed pair was verified, so phonetic compatibility should be described as supported by traditional lexicographic derivation plus later structural analysis, not as a demonstrated reconstructed sound equation.

No glyph image was visually inspected. No exact evidence was found for when an irregular graphic variant with 奈 arose; MOE identifies it as a variant and records shape substitution, but the history of that spelling remains limited.
No permission or editorial case for a versioned bulk extract was checked; this research relies on concise paraphrases and character-specific citations, with no mirrored source material.
No image of an ancient or manuscript form for 哪 was verified. The selected Commons candidate is a modern stroke-order drawing, useful only as a present-day graph reference.
Xiaoxuetang lookup endpoints failed through the web tool; no exact record image URL, record page, or image-specific evidence was available. The database homepage alone cannot establish a form for 哪.

MOE reports absence from 說文 and cites later lexicographic testimony that 哪 was originally 那, but this research did not independently inspect the cited 集韻 scan or establish a dated early manuscript witness for 哪.

The result-page suggestion of historical 哪 forms on general character-form websites was not adopted: relevant exact pages and provenance were not verified. No image from chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw was selected.

Official Unicode per-character pages for both 哪 and 那 failed to open in this invocation. The supplied local Unihan rows were considered as local evidence only; no externally verified Unihan page is claimed.

The queried web sources do not establish a reconstructed 哪 reading paired with 那. Local Baxter–Sagart data provides *nˤar for 那 but no 哪 row; current Mandarin readings alone do not establish the historical phonetic relation.

The Ministry of Education entry documents interrogative use of 那 (nǎ) in cited Tang and Song works, but does not show that those occurrences were written 哪. The start date for the 哪 spelling remains unresolved.
The official Unicode per-character record for 那 remained inaccessible. The supplied local Unihan row gives nà, but is local data rather than an externally inspected Unicode page.

The supplied local Baxter–Sagart data has 那 MC na and OC *nˤar, but no corresponding 哪 reconstruction. The present-day comparison nǎ–nà does not establish the historical basis or chronology of the phonetic analysis.

The separately attested readings nuó and nǎ for 那 are dictionary readings with distinct historical or lexical uses; the inspected evidence does not establish either as the relevant sound value in the 哪 compound. The corrected present-day comparison therefore uses principal readings nǎ for 哪 and nà for 那.
